newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: SOCCER-CONNOLLY SCORES THREE AS IRELAND WIN 5-0.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CONNOLLY SCORES THREE AS IRELAND WIN 5-0.

text.p: Teenage striker David Connolly scored a first-half hat-trick as Ireland beat little Liechtenstein 5-0 in a World Cup European group eight qualifying match on Wednesday.

Striker Tony Cascarino, who came on as a substitute for midfielder Ray Houghton in the 54th minute, helped himself to two headed goals to propel Ireland into second spot behind runaway group leaders Romania as Liechtenstein suffered their seventh defeat in seven games.

Connolly, 19, opened the scoring in the 28th minute when he chipped into an empty net from six metres after midfielder Roy Keane had drawn the attention of two defenders and goalkeeper Martin Heeb with a run inside the Liechtenstein penalty area.
He scored his second seven minutes later when he ran on to a brilliant through-pass from captain Andy Townsend and slotted the ball home low to Heeb's left.

Connolly completed his hat-trick in the 41st minute with his fifth international goal in six appearances. He got on the end of a cross-cum-shot by Townsend and tapped the ball home from point-blank range.
Cascarino, who plays for French club Nancy, added two more goals in the 60th and 78th minutes, receiving deep crosses from defender Jeff Kenna and sending searing headers into the roof of the net.
Romania top the group with maximum 18 points from six matches. Ireland moved ahead of Macedonia on goal difference. Both have 10 points from six games.
Liechtenstein remain bottom of the six-team group without a point from seven matches, having conceded 36 goals and scored just two.
